To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the diffusion of colloidal particles in a microfluidic channel is affected by both the flow shear rate and the proximity of channel walls, (2) the shear-induced collisions are the dominant effect for Pe > 10, (3) the walls cause a strong reduction in the self-diffusion coefficients, (4) the shear-induced diffusion enhancement is more pronounced in the flow direction than in the direction perpendicular to the walls, and (5) the diffusion enhancement is stronger for more concentrated

(1) in dilute suspensions (volume fraction of particles φ ≤ 0.1) shear does not affect the diffusion of the particles and (2) in concentrated suspensions (φ ≥ 0.3) shear induces a significant increase in the diffusion of particles.

the self-diffusion coefficient of colloidal suspensions flowing in microchannels is strongly reduced by the presence of walls, but is increased by the shear flow, especially in the flow (streamwise) direction.

in microchannels, the diffusion coefficients of colloidal particles are affected by the shear rate, and the walls.
